answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake tokens that are locked and slashed on provable misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Think of a jetty: only ships that pay the docking fee and prove their cargo can berth, while the rest wait outside. Each agent carries a unique onyx badge, a hardware-backed credential bound to one device, and every claim is signed with a cipher that peers can verify, so duplicates are exposed when the same badge signs twice under different names.
